description: Converted sky travel, abyss, driftland, and reclamation origins.

entries.title: Skyfarer Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for characters raised aboard airships or in communities built around sky travel.
body: Skyfarers learn balance, watch discipline, weather reading, rope work, and crew etiquette before most people learn the shape of a road. Their first vessel often remains an emotional homeland even after the crew scatters.
The origin favors navigators, sailors, scouts, messengers, shipboard artisans, and anyone who treats open sky as familiar terrain rather than an exceptional hazard.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Balance and Spot. These are always class skills for the character.
Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Survival or Knowledge (nature) checks to predict aerial weather, identify ordinary wind hazards, or interpret air currents.
Trade specialty: Profession (air sailor) or Profession (navigator).
Starting package: A tattered regional route map, a weathered skycompass or ordinary compass, 50 feet of hemp rope, a safety harness, traveler’s clothing, and 10 gp.

Access feature — Eye of the Storm: After 10 minutes observing the sky, attempt a DC 15 Survival or Knowledge (nature) check to predict ordinary weather and dangerous winds for the next 24 hours along the current route. Magical anomalies generally require DC 20 or higher and provide only several hours of warning.

sections.heading: Character creation use
body: Select this origin at 1st level as the character’s single origin package. It does not consume a feat or replace ancestry or class features.
The GM may replace individual pieces of starting gear with setting-equivalent items of roughly equal value.
The origin’s access feature creates a credible route to information, shelter, audiences, or facilities. It does not guarantee cooperation or eliminate payment, law, reputation, or risk.

entries.title: Abyss Watcher Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for sentries and survivors trained to recognize dangers rising from the Eternal Abyss.
body: Abyss Watchers are shaped by long vigils near exposed edges, lower fortifications, wreck fields, and settlements that cannot afford a moment of complacency.
Their habits combine physical readiness, trap awareness, emergency signaling, and a grim respect for phenomena that ordinary travelers dismiss until too late.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Climb and Survival. These are always class skills for the character.

Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Search, Spot, or Survival checks made to detect abyssal creatures, abyss-linked tracks, structural edge hazards, traps near exposed drops, or magical phenomena associated with the Abyss.
Trade specialty: Choose Craft (trapmaking), Craft (stonemasonry), Profession (guard), or Profession (siege engineer).
Starting package: Sturdy boots, an etched skystone, a hunting trap, 50 feet of rope, a signal whistle, and 8 gp.

Access feature — Abyssal Warning: When entering a lower deck, exposed ledge, ruin, or abyss-facing fortification, the GM should allow one reactive Search or Survival check to notice an abyss-specific warning sign before the party fully commits to the danger. This is not automatic detection and does not reveal ordinary hidden threats.

entries.title: Driftlander Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for people raised on isolated drifting islands where self-sufficiency is a daily requirement.
body: Driftlanders learn to stretch stores, preserve water, recognize local plants, and repair what cannot be replaced. Isolation produces strong household bonds and a practical suspicion of waste.
A Driftlander may be curious about the wider world, but seldom assumes that trade, rescue, or replacement supplies will arrive on time.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Knowledge (nature) and Survival. These are always class skills for the character.
Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Survival checks to forage, locate water, preserve food, or improvise shelter on floating islands.
Trade specialty: Choose Craft (basketweaving), Craft (carpentry), Profession (herder), Profession (fisher), or Profession (farmer).
Starting package: Dried herbs, a carved household charm, a sky-fishing net, a utility knife, three days of preserved food, and 5 gp.

Access feature — Island Resilience: In nonbarren island terrain, a successful DC 10 Survival check provides food and water for the character; every 2 points by which the result exceeds 10 supports one additional creature, to a maximum of four creatures total. Severe scarcity, contamination, or unnatural ecology can increase the DC or make gathering impossible.

entries.title: Sky Reclaimer Origin
entries.summary: A converted origin for salvage workers, ruin delvers, wreck divers, and specialists who recognize value in abandoned machinery.
body: Sky Reclaimers recover components, maps, cargo, and artifacts from fallen ships and forgotten islands. Their journals blend routes, hazard marks, valuations, and arguments with previous owners.
Reclaimers learn that salvage is part archaeology, part engineering, part theft law, and part survival.

sections.heading: Converted Hypertext d20 origin package
body: Associated skills: Appraise and Search. These are always class skills for the character.
Origin focus: Gain a +2 origin bonus on Appraise, Search, or Craft checks made to identify valuable salvage, reusable components, structural access points, or the likely original purpose of wreckage.
Trade specialty: Choose Craft (mechanical), Profession (salvager), Profession (surveyor), or Disable Device as the origin specialty.
Starting package: A crowbar, salvage hammer, chalk, 50 feet of rope, a battered field journal, three empty specimen sacks, and 7 gp.

Access feature — Treasure Hunter’s Instinct: After spending 1 minute examining a wreck, ruin chamber, or debris field, the character may attempt an Appraise or Search check. DC 15 identifies the most obviously valuable recoverable category; DC 20 also identifies one concealed danger, ownership mark, or high-value component if present.
